title: Add support for customizing the value of DonutSummary

complexity.rationale: The two sites (vega-spec-builder and vega-spec-builder-s2's donutSummaryUtils.ts) are near-identical files, so applying the fix to both is a repeated, precedented edit on its own. But there is a genuine open design question — should the override be a static number, or should it be able to reference/select a specific slice's value from the data — and resolving `getSummaryValueText`'s current hardcoded dependence on the `sum` aggregate field (not just swapping a prop) is new, non-precedented logic, which is what pushes this past a 2.

summary: DonutSummary's center value always displays the sum of all slices' metric values, computed via an unconditional aggregate transform (packages/vega-spec-builder/src/donut/donutSummaryUtils.ts:69-88 and the identical logic in packages/vega-spec-builder-s2/src/donut/donutSummaryUtils.ts) with no override. This request adds a way to show an arbitrary or single-slice value instead (e.g. `<DonutSummary value={someValue}/>`), for cases like displaying a score out of 10 rather than a sum.
requirements: Add an optional `value` field to DonutSummaryOptions (packages/vega-spec-builder/src/types/marks/supplemental/dountSummarySpec.types.ts and the s2 mirror) that, when provided, overrides the computed sum.

When `value` is set, `getSummaryValueText` (donutSummaryUtils.ts) must use it directly instead of the `sum` field from the `${donutOptions.name}_summaryData` aggregate source, while still applying `numberFormat` via the existing getTextNumberFormat helper.
When `value` is not set, behavior is unchanged (sum of all slice values, as today).
The override must work identically for both vega-spec-builder (s1) and vega-spec-builder-s2, since DonutSummary's implementation is duplicated near-verbatim between the two packages.
isBoolean donut summaries (which already compute a percent from a single datum) are unaffected by this change — `value` only applies to the non-boolean summary path.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Renders '0' (formatted per numberFormat), not treated as falsy/omitted — distinguish from `value` being undefined.
hideValue still takes precedence and no value text mark is added, consistent with existing getDonutSummaryGroupMark logic.
Layout (baseline, limit, font-size) is unaffected by where the number came from — reuse existing getSummaryValueBaseline/getSummaryValueLimit unchanged.
`value` is ignored (or documented as unsupported) since the boolean path already derives its own percent text from a single datum field.
Both vega-spec-builder/src/donut/donutSummaryUtils.ts and vega-spec-builder-s2/src/donut/donutSummaryUtils.ts must resolve `value` the same way.

crossCutting.notes: variant is 'both' because this spec's implementationPlan already covers the identical change in both vega-spec-builder and vega-spec-builder-s2 from the outset, so there is no separate 'other variant' to flag via requiresS1S2Parity.

implementationPlan.change: Add optional `value?: number` to DonutSummaryOptions with JSDoc explaining it overrides the computed sum.

In getSummaryValueText, if options.value is defined, use it as a literal value (via numeric formula/value ref) instead of `{ field: 'sum' }`; leave getSummaryValueEncode/getDonutSummaryData otherwise unchanged.
Mirror the identical change to getSummaryValueText.
Passes through automatically via Omit<DonutSummaryOptions, ...> since `value` is a plain value prop; verify no existing Omit conflicts.
Mirror the same verification for the s2 Props type.
Destructure `value` alongside numberFormat/hideValue/label so Storybook picks up the new prop default (undefined).
Document the new `value` prop on DonutSummary with the score-out-of-10 example from the issue.
Add a story showing a custom `value` overriding the sum.

openQuestions: Should `value` accept only a static number, or should it also support selecting a specific slice's value from the chart data (e.g. by matching a color/category key), as one of the issue's use cases ("just one slice's value") implies?
Should `value` be validated/typed as ignored when isBoolean=true, or should it throw/warn?
